episode.title: Centralize project trust policy and isolate executable project effects
episode.before: At parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84, trust decisions applied only to the exact working directory; project instruction files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md triggered approval and were hidden when untrusted; interactive startup contained its own trust-resolution logic; package and config commands used separate, simpler rules and could not consult project_trust extensions or a configurable global default.
episode.after: At d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd, passive project instruction files load regardless of trust, while approval is required only for project configuration or discovered skill directories. Trust decisions inherit from the nearest ancestor and may be persisted for a parent folder or limited to the session. A shared resolver applies explicit override, safe-input bypass, extension decision, persisted decision, global default, and fail-closed prompting in order. Interactive startup, package commands, and config commands use this resolver after a bootstrap pass that excludes project-local executable resources.
episode.diff: The change adds shared project-trust and startup-UI modules; extends the trust store with ancestor lookup, atomic multi-path updates, parent-folder choices, and saved-source reporting; narrows trust-input detection and ungates context-file loading; adds global ask/always/never policy; and routes normal startup plus package/config commands through the same trust-resolution pipeline. Tests cover inheritance and override clearing, passive instruction visibility, global-default precedence, extension-mediated package trust, and persisted-decision precedence.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit resolves PR #5549 as an implementation-bearing change titled "feat(ui): Improved project approval settings" with 26 coding-agent files changed.

Before the change, hasProjectTrustInputs treated AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in the directory ancestry as approval-triggering inputs, and ProjectTrustStore.get read only the exact normalized working-directory key.
After the change, trust-input detection checks the current project's .pi directory and ancestral .agents/skills directories, but no longer treats AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md as trust-gated inputs.
Project context loading no longer accepts a projectTrusted flag and always collects context files from the working directory and its ancestors.
The resource-loader regression test proves that an untrusted project still exposes its AGENTS.md while extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and project settings remain excluded.

The trust store normalizes paths, walks toward the filesystem root to find the nearest explicit decision, reports the source path, and supports locked multi-path updates that can delete child overrides.
Trust choices now include trusting the current folder, trusting its parent while clearing the current override, session-only allow/deny choices, and persistent denial.
Trust-manager tests prove nearest-ancestor inheritance, child override precedence, and restoration of parent inheritance after atomically clearing the child override.
Trust-selector tests prove inherited-decision labeling and that selecting parent trust returns coordinated parent-save and child-clear updates.

The shared resolver orders trust policy as explicit override, automatic approval when no gated inputs exist, extension hook, persisted nearest-path decision, global ask/always/never default, and finally UI selection or fail-closed denial when no UI or selection is available.
The global settings manager exposes defaultProjectTrust with ask as the fallback for absent or invalid values and persists changes only in global settings.
Settings tests prove that project-local settings cannot override the global default trust policy and that invalid values resolve to ask.
The resource loader provides a bootstrap pass that forces untrusted settings before loading only the current safe extension set, then reloads full resources after trust resolution.

Package and config commands construct an initially untrusted settings manager, optionally load bootstrap trust extensions, invoke the shared resolver, set the resulting trust state, report warnings, and block local package mutations when untrusted.
Normal application startup invokes the shared resolver with the global default, bootstrap extensions, UI context, and extension-error reporting before resource loading continues.

Package-command tests prove that the global always policy enables project packages, project_trust extensions can approve package commands, and an explicit trust-store denial overrides the global always policy.
The parent implementation embedded trust resolution in main and used a separate package-command rule, while the new implementation extracts the resolver and routes both command paths through it.

candidate_atomics.name: separate-passive-context-from-trust-gated-effects
candidate_atomics.description: Classify passive instruction loading separately from project resources that can execute code, install packages, or alter runtime behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Keep useful project instructions available without granting permission for executable or configuration-driven project effects.
semantic_action.pre_state: Passive instruction files and effect-bearing project resources share one trust gate, so denying effects also removes contextual instructions.
semantic_action.post_state: Passive context remains readable while settings, packages, extensions, skills, prompts, and themes remain governed by project trust.
semantic_action.validation: The untrusted-resource test observes the project AGENTS.md and simultaneously observes that trust-gated resources and settings are absent.

candidate_atomics.name: inherit-nearest-ancestor-trust-with-explicit-overrides
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve trust from the closest persisted ancestor and support coordinated updates that establish parent policy while removing a narrower override.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a user to approve or deny a directory tree without losing the ability to override a nested project.
semantic_action.pre_state: Trust is stored and retrieved only for an exact project path, requiring repetitive decisions for related directories.
semantic_action.post_state: The closest explicit path decision governs descendants, and clearing a child decision deterministically restores ancestor inheritance.
semantic_action.validation: Store tests exercise parent inheritance, nearer child precedence, and child-clear restoration; selector tests verify the coordinated update payload.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-trust-through-one-precedence-policy
candidate_atomics.description: Apply all trust inputs through a single fail-closed decision order.

semantic_action.intent: Produce one deterministic trust result across interactive and non-interactive execution while preserving explicit user and extension decisions.
semantic_action.pre_state: Trust behavior is distributed across entry points and lacks a configurable global default with explicit precedence.
semantic_action.post_state: Explicit override wins first; harmless projects bypass prompting; extension and persisted decisions precede the global default; unresolved ask mode prompts only with UI and otherwise denies.
semantic_action.validation: Settings tests establish default parsing and scope; package-command tests establish default approval, extension approval, and persisted denial precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: bootstrap-trust-hooks-without-loading-project-effects
candidate_atomics.description: Load only non-project and injected trust-decision extensions before approval, then apply the resulting decision before exposing project resources.

semantic_action.intent: Permit policy extensions to participate in approval without executing the untrusted project's own extensions or packages first.
semantic_action.pre_state: A command either cannot consult trust extensions or risks loading project-local effects before trust is established.
semantic_action.post_state: The bootstrap phase is forced untrusted, trust hooks may decide policy, and full project resources are loaded only after the decision is installed.
semantic_action.validation: The package-command extension test approves a project package through an injected project_trust hook, while the implementation explicitly forces untrusted settings for the bootstrap load.

candidate_workflows.name: centralize-and-enforce-project-effect-approval
candidate_workflows.description: Refine an overbroad project approval boundary, represent scoped decisions, resolve them through one precedence contract, and safely reuse that contract at every effect-bearing entry point.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow passive project context while consistently preventing unapproved project-controlled effects across startup and command entry points.
workflow_graph.entry_state: One coarse trust gate suppresses both instructions and executable resources; decisions are exact-path only; and entry points implement divergent approval logic.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Only effect-bearing project inputs require approval, scoped decisions inherit predictably, all entry points share one fail-closed resolver, and pre-approval hooks execute without loading project-local effects.
unresolved_or_deferred: The bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, or status-check results, so the maintainers' stated rationale and CI outcome cannot be established.
The pinned tests were inspected as validation oracles but were not executed during this extraction.
Cross-repository pattern induction and holdout promotion are deferred because this episode supplies only one repository workflow.

unresolved_questions: Whether loading project instruction files without trust was motivated solely by their passive nature or by a broader compatibility requirement is not documented in the available GitHub evidence.
No direct unit test isolates every branch of resolveProjectTrusted; branch behavior is established from implementation plus integration tests for the main precedence cases.
The issue bundle lists unrelated files from other merge activity, so episode evidence is restricted to the first-parent diff from 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84 to the pinned merge commit.
